metadata.architecture: single-head causal retrieval with compact tied representation
metadata.author: declarative architecture search
metadata.mechanism_hypothesis: A single eight-dimensional attention head can encode the symmetric operand-digit combination without fragmenting retrieval across heads, preserving eligibility with fewer parameters.
metadata.name: Single-Head Bottleneck Addition Decoder
metadata.research_alternative_explanation: One shared attention distribution may encode the unordered pair of aligned operand digits more efficiently than two separate low-dimensional heads.
metadata.research_challenged_assumption: The current direction assumes two attention heads are useful for operand retrieval despite having no positive public score.
metadata.research_current_explanation: The parent uses two five-dimensional heads so separate attention patterns can retrieve operand information before tied readout.
metadata.research_decision_rule: Accept only if validity and the public eligibility floor are preserved with fewer trusted parameters; use public accuracy only for an exact parameter-count tie.
metadata.research_discriminating_evidence: Preserved or improved eligibility would favor unified retrieval; a loss relative to the parent would favor distinct multi-head operand access.
metadata.research_evidence: The parent scored 0.000000 publicly, so there is no decisive evidence that splitting its representation across two heads aids addition.
metadata.research_expected_result: Unified attention over eight channels should retain the parent eligibility level while reducing embedding and attention parameters.
metadata.research_next_experiment: Replace the ten-dimensional two-head attention geometry with one eight-dimensional head while preserving the remaining information flow.
metadata.research_previous_interpretation: The attention-only parent produced no positive public score, leaving its two-head retrieval assumption unsupported.
